summary_paragraph: A man with end-stage renal disease, type 2 diabetes, chronic systolic heart failure, and atrial fibrillation was admitted with a 5-day history of generalized weakness and 1 day of shortness of breath. He had missed a scheduled blood transfusion and increased fluid intake prior to admission. On evaluation, he showed signs of fluid overload with bilateral pulmonary edema on imaging. He underwent hemodialysis with removal of 4.5 liters of fluid, leading to resolution of dyspnea. He received one unit of packed red blood cells for anemia, with improvement in symptoms. An echocardiogram revealed moderate right ventricular dysfunction and pulmonary hypertension but preserved left ventricular function. He experienced transient atrial flutter with rapid ventricular response after restarting diltiazem, which was managed with a single oral dose. His heart rate stabilized, and he was discharged home in stable condition with home physical therapy, instructions to monitor daily weight, and plans to evaluate for occult gastrointestinal bleeding.
problems: Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage V or end stage renal disease
